title: L1 recommendation graph document
description: One L1 graph: publications, recommendations and the citations that point at them, as typed nodes and reified edges. This schema checks form only -- tier 1. It cannot check that a node's type is a class the ontology declares, nor that an edge is a triple the ontology licenses, because both live in ontology/l1.json rather than in this file; that is tier 2, and tools/validate.mjs is the reference implementation. A document passing this schema and failing that check is a well-formed graph of things the model does not say.

@context.description: The context published beside this schema, by URL or inline. A graph carrying its own ad-hoc context is not interoperable with the rest of the WHO linked-data estate, which is the point of having one.

id.description: IRI of this graph document. One document is one DAK at one version.

type.description: prov:Entity. The document is a provenance-tracked thing, matching how smart-base stamps its generated JSON-LD vocabularies.

ontologyVersion.description: schemaVersion of the ontology/l1.json this graph was built against. A graph outliving its ontology is why this is recorded rather than assumed.

wasDerivedFrom.description: The DAK sources this graph was extracted from, each pinned by hash. Same doctrine as the audit sidecar: edit a source and everything derived from it goes stale on its own rather than quietly disagreeing.

dak.description: The DAK envelope itself — the fields of the smart-base DAK logical model. Kept out of nodes because it is the subject of the whole document rather than one thing in it.

classId.description: An ontology class id -- "recommendation", "terminology-code". Membership is checked at tier 2 against ontology/l1.json; this only rules out ids that could never be one.

predicate.description: A predicate name. Membership is checked at tier 2 against ontology/l1.json; this only rules out strings that could never be one. Deliberately not an enum: the predicate set belongs to the ontology and changes with it, so a list here would be a second copy that drifts.

derivation.description: Identical to traceability-link.schema.json, deliberately. derived: mechanically produced, no choice involved. inferred: a rule that could reasonably have gone another way. decided: the source is silent and someone chose. Every node and edge in a graph is one of the three, and the third is the one a reviewer needs to find.

evidence.description: Where this came from in the DAK. Required on anything not mechanically derived, for the same reason a failing check must quote its source: an assertion with nothing to point at is the confident wrong answer the package exists to prevent.

location.description: file:line, a spreadsheet sheet and cell, or a BPMN element id.

artifact.description: The generated artifact affected, where one exists.

nodeProperties.description: Instance fields. The permitted keys per class are declared on the class in ontology/l1.json and checked at tier 2; nothing is asserted about them here.

label.description: Human-readable name. Required so a retrieved node reads without resolving it.

definedBy.description: Canonical URL of the smart-base logical model giving this node's instance shape, where the class has one. Ten of the nineteen concepts have none; those carry an id, a label and their edges, and nothing about their contents can be validated.

flagRef.description: Id of a flag raised while extracting this node. The flag itself lives in the extracting skill's validation report, not in the graph: a graph records what it found and what it had to decide, and routing an open question to its owner is the authoring pipeline's job.

skill.description: Skill id that produced this node.

then.description: A node that was not mechanically derived must say why it is what it is and point at the source. Without both, the record is no better than no record.

edge.description: One reified statement. Reified rather than written as a plain node property because an edge here carries a qualifier, a derivation and its evidence, and a plain property has nowhere to put them.

source.description: IRI of a node in this document.

target.description: IRI of a node in this document.

qualifier.description: The relationship label from the ArchiMate model — "use", "has", "participate", "applies to". It is the difference between a Business Process using a Data Object and having a Requirement, and dropping it flattens the model to bare adjacency.
